answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making every identity lock a refundable deposit that is only released after peer-checked work across several epochs, so trust accumulates like a onyx settling over a timber and following the opal of verified jobs instead of instant signups. One honest agent locks one deposit and does one stream of real work. An attacker spinning up a thousand fakes must lock a thousand deposits and perform a thousand streams of checked work, and if the fakes misbehave the deposits are slashed, so the swarm costs far more than honest participation ever pays.
